dedupe_keys.name: global daily evapotranspiration deficit index dedi 0 25 degree 1979 2020

description: DEDI is a daily drought index computed from daily actual and potential evapotranspiration from the ERA5 reanalysis of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, on a 0.25 by 0.25 degree grid for 1979 to 2020. The DataCite record says it was used to trace four 2019 spring and summer droughts in China, where it captured onset, end and multiple intensity peaks better than the operational Meteorological drought Composite Index and SPEI, and that it reflects vegetation and land surface conditions so it can support agricultural as well as meteorological drought monitoring. It was published by the listed authors in Science Data Bank (version 4, updated December 2021) under the CC BY 4.0 licence, free to download as 43 files of about 50 GB. Coverage is global. Caveats: the file format is not stated on the page read, the validation shown is for China, and it inherits ERA5 biases. For simulation it gives a daily global drought hazard series for crop loss, supply chain and water demand scenarios. Related catalogue records include the ERA5 reanalysis and the EDO Combined Drought Indicator.
name: Global Daily Evapotranspiration Deficit Index (DEDI), 0.25 degree, 1979-2020
